items.title: Joe Wilder Part 2 interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 12, 1998
items.q: And Pete said he’s sitting there and he’s almost like almost pale.

ctx.x: Well yes I did, and even while I was with the band I always practiced a lot of classical things, not thinking that I would ever get an opportunity to play in a symphony orchestra, but I just did it because of my interest in that. And when I was younger I heard Del Staigers , who, he’s one, and I’m sure I heard Herbert Clarke and Walter Smith, people like that who were very famous cornet soloists. But I remember Del Staigers for some reason or other better than the others, and I always wanted to play like Del…

he did that. He brought them in. So I took it home and it was Del Staigers , and he had a very high pitched voice “and now when you do this —” you do so and so and so and so. He had a voice like that. But his playing was really beautiful. And of course the recording wasn’t that great because of the time at which it was done. So I thought to myself, now what can I do to put Dick Perry on when I go back with these recordings? And I had one of these big LP’s on rubber about that thick, those old recordings, it was…
Yeah, I’ve learned that you’re quite a practical joker. Bob Rosengarden was saying, he called them “Wilderisms” that you used to do on the Dick Cavett band?
